topic: Night of the Grizzlies -- two women killed by different grizzlies the same night in Glacier National Park (1967), caused by hotel bear-feeding shows and a failed huckleberry crop
title: Two Grizzlies Killed Two Women In One Night, Ten Miles Apart
description: AI-narrated original commentary on the 1967 'Night of the Grizzlies' in Glacier National Park -- the night two different grizzly bears killed two different women in two different locations, and the hotel bear-feeding shows that helped cause it. Not sourced from any single video; written as original commentary on a public historical event.

hook_candidates.text: Two different grizzly bears each killed a different woman on the exact same night, ten miles apart.
How do two separate grizzly bear attacks happen in the same park on the exact same night?
The bears that killed two women in one night weren't hunting on instinct. Tourists had trained them to expect food.
Julie Helgeson and Michele Koons never met, but they died the same night, ten miles apart, killed by two different grizzlies.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who insists wild animal attacks are just random bad luck, because they want to prove humans usually cause it.
contradicted_belief: Most people assume two grizzly bears attacking on the same night is just wild coincidence.
closing_comment: Julie and Michele never met, but two grizzlies killing them the same night is why every national park closed its bear-feeding dumps.

sources.note: Confirms two women killed by separate grizzlies the same night, Aug 12-13 1967, ~10 miles apart, first fatal attacks in park history.
Confirms hotel garbage-dump bear-feeding shows and the nationwide closure of open-pit park dumps that followed.
